The frequency and topographic distribution of Lymph Node Metastases (LNM) are not modified by Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy (NACT) in cervical cancer. However, clinical non-responders showed more involved LNs. As a result, a systemic and extensive lymphadenectomy should be performed in patients treated with NACT plus surgery regardless of the response to NACT.

This means that while neoadjuvant chemotherapy may reduce the number of lymph nodes involved, it does not alter their frequency or distribution. Instead, a more comprehensive lymphadenectomy is still necessary for all patients undergoing treatment with NACT and subsequent surgery, even if they respond to chemotherapy.
